Karbala
hook: There was no pledge of allegiance to Yazid. The water was cut off. On the tenth of Muharram, the Ahl al-Bayt were martyred.
scenes.0.text: When Mu'awiya died, his son Yazid succeeded him. The governor of Medina, W**alid**, summoned Husayn to his palace and asked him to make a vow to Yazid. A pledge of allegiance to a ruler. Everyone knew what kind of man Yazid was: he drank wine, played monkey, played with dogs and hunted, didn't mind praying. His grandfather Abu Sufyan waged war against Islam for years, his grandmother was remembered for what she did to the body of Hazrat **Hamza** at **Hind** Uhud, and his father Mu'awiya had drawn a sword against Hazrat Ali. The Prophet said of Husayn and his brother **Hasan**, "the masters of the youth of Paradise". Hasan made peace with Mu'awiya and was then martyred by poisoning. Now a ruler from the same family expected the Prophet's remaining grandson to submit. Looking at the governor's face, Husayn replied: "Yazid is a pervert. He drinks wine and kills innocent souls whom God has sanctified. A man like me doesn't care about a man like him". Then he got up and left the palace.

scenes.1.text: A few nights later, when the streets of Medina were buried in silence, Husayn prepared his family for the journey. His sister, Zaynab, was with him, and the little children were sleepy-eyed in their mother's arms. He went to his grandfather's grave before he left. He bowed to the Prophet's grave and stayed there for a long time. Her lips were moving, tears streaming from her eyes. As he said goodbye to his grandfather, he said: "Grandfather, they're calling me. I'm going too". The ground was cool, and a gentle breeze was blowing from the palm trees. When the caravan left Medina in the dark, the houses of the city were slowly left behind. He was on his way to Mecca, and he would never again see the city where Husayn was born and raised.

scenes.2.text: It was the season of Umrah in Mecca, and the area around the Kaaba was crowded. During the days when Husayn was staying there, letters began to come from Kufa. A few came first, then the back didn't. They all had the same call: "O grandson of the Prophet! We don't accept the caliphate of someone like Yazid. Come, be our caliph, and we will pledge to you". The Kufars did not call him their governor, but the caliph of the Ummah instead of Yazid. His Holiness did not immediately respond to this call. He first sent his uncle's son Muslim b. Aqil to Kufa to see the real state of the city. When he reached the Muslim Qufa, the houses rushed to receive him. Thousands of people held out their hands and pledged allegiance to him in the name of His Holiness. For several days, the name of the Ahl al-Bayt was mentioned with joy in the streets of Kufa. In Mecca, Husayn was waiting for news from his uncle's son.

scenes.3.text: That joy didn't last long. Yazid sent Ubaydullah b. Ziyad to Kufa as governor. As soon as Ibn Ziyad entered the city, he caused panic and the doors were closed one by one. Yesterday's Muslims locked their doors this time. When evening came, Muslim b. Aqil was alone in the city of thousands of people who had promised him. After a while, he was captured and taken to the palace. He was martyred on the orders of Ibn Ziyad and his head was sent to Yazid. Husayn was unaware of what was happening. He had already left Mecca with his family and was on his way to Iraq, to the city that was calling him. There were others who joined the convoy along the way, but they didn't yet know that Kufe had gone silent.

scenes.4.text: These are the events that happened before the Muslim was martyred. Ibn Ziyad's soldiers surrounded the house where he was hiding to capture him. He was wounded by Muslim in a raid while trying to capture him and was eventually captured. When he was brought to the palace gate, his face was covered in blood and his lips were dry from thirst. There was a pitcher of cold water by the door. He asked for a sip of water. A man named **Muslim b. Amr** wouldn't give him a drop and told him he couldn't drink from this water without tasting hellfire. Soon afterwards, **Amr b. Hureys** took pity on her and had water brought. The Muslim took the cup to his lips. But the blood from the wounds on his face when he was taken captive, dripped into the cup, and the water turned to blood. The bowl was refilled, and the same thing happened again. The Muslim refused to drink the water contaminated with his own blood and put the cup back. So the grandson of the Prophet's uncle was taken into the palace thirsty and was martyred there thirsty. A few weeks later, his uncle's son, Husayn, was to be martyred on the banks of the Euphrates, without water, despite a river flowing before his eyes.

scenes.5.text: As the convoy moved through the Iraqi desert, a cloud of dust appeared on the horizon at noon. The arrival was a thousand horsemen under the command of Hürr b. Yazid er-Riyâhi. Their mission was to stop the convoy and divert it. The sun was high, the horses had foam in their mouths, and the soldiers' lips cracked from thirst. When Husayn saw their condition, he told his youths to open the water jars. First he watered the soldiers, then the horses. He'd water an army that came to stop him, and he wouldn't turn anyone away. The Hürr was surprised by this generosity. Then Husayn recited a sermon to them: "You invited me. I still have your letters". Hürr did not draw his sword, but he did not back down from his orders. The two communities walked side by side in the same dust.

scenes.6.text: On the second day of Muharram, the horses stopped in a desert and didn't take another step. His Holiness Husayn asked me the name of this place. They said, "The Karbala". This name meant sorrow and trouble. The Prophet had announced the name of the place where his grandson would be martyred years ago. He also entrusted a handful of land brought by Gabriel to **Ummu Seleme**, saying that when this land turned to blood, he would understand that Husayn was martyred. Husayn got off his horse and said, "This is a place of curse and trouble. Stay, our blood will be shed here". He purchased the desert from the people of Nineveh and Gadiriah for sixty thousand dirhams, and then pardoned them on the condition that they guide the visitors to his tomb and provide them with three days' hospitality. They pitched their tents on the banks of the Euphrates. Soon Umar b. Sa'd arrived with a large army. He was promised the governorship of Rey in exchange for this job.

scenes.7.text: On the seventh day of Muharram, a new order came from Kufa: not a drop of water would reach the tents of Husayn. Umar b. Sa'd took the Euphrates bank with his horsemen. The river flowed right by the tents. It was heard at night, and a cool mist rose over it in the morning. But drinking that water was forbidden. The soldiers of the opposing army were watering their horses in the same river. And the Prophet's grandchildren couldn't get near that shore. This ban was ordered by Yazid's governor in Kufa and an army loyal to Muawi's son gave the Prophet's family a sip of water. Three days to Ashura.

scenes.8.text: The nights after the water was cut off, the tents were filled with stifling heat. The whip was empty, the container was upside down. The kids were looking for something to wet their dry lips. The mothers tried to put them to sleep by rocking them in their arms, keeping their voices low. Husayn's tents moved one by one. He caressed the head of a crying child, wished a mother patience. He was as quiet as anyone, but he didn't show it on his face. The roar of the Euphrates was still heard in the darkness. The watchmen's torches burned like a chain along the shore. The water was just a few feet away, and there was a whole army in between. By morning, the children's lips were even cracked.

scenes.9.text: On the ninth day of Muharram, on Thursday evening, Shimr b. Zil-Javshen came to the front of the tents and called out loudly, "Where are the sons of my sister?" He meant the sons of Umm al-Benin and their brothers. **Abbas** was the son of **Ali**. His mother was Umm al-Benin, and the mother of Husayn was **Fatimah**. Their mothers were different, but their fathers were the same. I mean, Abbas was a brother of Husayn's father. He was a tall, strong and very handsome young man. Because of her beauty, she was called Kamer-i Beni Hashim, which means the moon of the sons of Hashem. But what really made him famous was his loyalty. Abbas never saw his brother Husayn as separate from himself. He would call him "sir" instead of "brother", carry his banner and follow him like his shadow. Zimri was of the same family as their mother. He had a bail bond. Aman is a promise of safety. Shimr spoke on behalf of Yazid: "Do not die with Husayn. You will not be touched". The youths came forward and said, "May Allah curse you and your trust. Do you trust us with the son of God when we have no confidence in him?" Abbas added: "May your hands be dry. Should we obey the damned and not our brother Husayn?" Then he tore up the deposit slip and threw it away. Zimri returned empty-handed to his army.

scenes.10.text: It was Zaynab who ran the most in the tents that evening. She was the daughter of Ali and Fatima and she carried the burden of the family in Karbala. He took the children who were crying in fear and sat them at the bottom of his robe. He spoke words that made them forget their thirst, took them by the hand, and wiped their tears. Her own heart trembled for her brother, yet she kept her voice still because the children's eyes were on her face. He went from tent to tent encouraging the women. He stopped by his sick nephew's and wiped the sweat off his forehead. As the night progressed, most of the little ones fell asleep in her arms. The next morning, many of these children would lose their father, uncle, or brother.

scenes.11.text: There was a young man among them who was very sick. Husayn's son, Zayn al-Abidin, was lying in a corner of the tent in the flames. He had no strength to go to war, and his illness kept him away from the square of Karbala. In later years, he would recount that evening: the night before his father was to be martyred, he was sitting sick in his bed, and his aunt, Zaynab, was waiting at the head and looking after him. God's destiny did not include this young man among the martyrs, but among the survivors. After Assyria, there would be those who would kill him, who would say, "That sickness is enough for him". His illness did not save him from the captivity of the Kufa and Damascus. But he survived as the Imam of the Prophet's line and returned to Medina years later.

scenes.12.text: That night, Umar b. Sa'd gave them till the morning. He gathered Husayn's friends in a big tent. The fuse of the candle was burning dimly. He lifted their beads from them and said, "Enjoy the darkness of the night and go. You don't have to stay with me. Yazid only wants me". Many of those who had gone in the hope of the booty had already dispersed when they heard that the Kufa had fallen and that Muslim had been martyred. A few more left that night in the dark. And the rest of them didn't move. **Abbas** was the first to speak: "If I were to be killed a thousand times and resurrected, I would never leave you". **Muslim b. Avsece** and Zuhayr b. Kayn made the same promise. The rest of the night, the sound of the Quran, prayer and praise went up from the tents. The foreheads bowed, the swords waited in their sheaths. By morning, only seventy-two warriors remained with Husayn. These seventy-two men were to fight in the cause of Allah against an army of a thousand. He knew that death was certain and inevitable, but he did not turn away from this path to please God. For him, it was more a matter of a dignified death than a vow to someone like Yazid, and his words to the enemy army on the day of Assyria were: "Heyhaat minne'z-zille", which means "Shame is far from us".
scenes.12.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj

scenes.13.text: On the tenth day of Muharram, the morning of Ashura, the sun rose in a red light over the desert. He mounted Husayn's horse and went into the gap between the two armies. Thousands of soldiers lined up in front of him. His voice was heard through the dust: "Don't you recognize me? I am the grandson of the Messenger of Allah. My father is Ali, my mother is Fatima". He reminded them of the Prophet's words about him and his brother, "the masters of the youths of Paradise". Some soldiers in the opposite line bowed their heads, some lost their eyes. Husayn spoke so effectively, rightly and truthfully that the commanders feared that the soldiers would be influenced and change their line. Many of the soldiers in the front began to whistle and shout at the order they had received. So they tried to suppress Husayn's voice and prevent the soldiers behind him from hearing him. But as soon as the sermon was finished, the commanders signalled the archers and the bows began to tense. That morning, two armies were facing each other in the same desert: on one side, the reign of Yazid, and on the other, a family that had been waiting for three days without water.
scenes.13.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj

scenes.14.text: On his way back from the sermon, Husayn got off his horse and stood for a while in front of the tents. Zaynab was waiting by the door with a little boy clinging to her skirt. Women and girls were looking at him from behind the curtains. Husayn looked at each of them in the face. He didn't talk long. There was love and goodbye in her eyes. She went back to her sister and put her in the care of the children. Zaynab shook her head, wiped her tears with her hand. After that morning, he was to protect the children, the women and his sick nephew. When Husayn got back on his horse, the boy still had not removed his aunt's skirt.

scenes.15.text: Just as the battle was about to begin, a man in the enemy ranks began to tremble. It was **Hürr** who stopped the convoy on the way. Those with him saw his face turn yellow. Hürr pulled his horse and said, "I find myself between heaven and hell". Then he chose paradise. He saddles his horse and crosses the gap between his two armies. When he reached Husayn, he got off his horse and bowed his head before him and said, "I was the one who kept you on the road. Will my repentance be accepted?" His Holiness has forgiven him. Hürr fought in the front lines, facing the army to which he had just belonged, and was martyred that morning. Husayn came to his head, wiped the dust off his face and said, "You are free, and your mother gave birth to you free.

scenes.16.text: Then one by one, Husayn's friends began to appear. **Habib b. Muzahir** was one of Ali's old friends. He had a white beard, but he fought like a young man in the arena. Zuhayr b. Cain had joined the caravan when returning from the pilgrimage and stood in front of Husayn until his sword fell from his hand. The story of a young man named **Vehb** is also told in the Ahl-i Beyt narratives. As his mother sent him out, she said, "My son, stand before the Prophet's grandson". When Vehb returned from the square, his mother sent him back, and he was martyred. Each went by his own name, each with his own story. With each martyr's death, the ranks in front of the tents became thinner, and by noon, the number of men who could fight was down to a handful.

scenes.17.text: When the sun reached its peak, Abu Summah reminded Husayn that it was time for his noon prayer. Husayn looked up at the sky and said, "Yes, it's time for prayer". He then asked the enemy to cease fighting so that they could pray. **Husayn b. Numeyr** mockingly shouted: "That prayer is not acceptable!" He said, "Would your prayer be accepted if it were not for the son of the Messenger of Allah?" According to Ahl al-Bayt, the commanders of the opposing side called out to their soldiers, "Raise the arrows and stop praying". There was a reason for that. Yazid's men portrayed Husayn as an apostate so that people could fight against the Prophet's grandson. They said he was an infidel because he didn't pledge allegiance to Yazid. If the soldiers saw him praying, they would ask among themselves, "If this man is praying, how can he be a heretic?" The commanders feared that such a split would arise within the army. Because at the beginning of the war, he had switched ranks from his commanders and joined Husayn. They didn't want anyone else to follow him. Husayn, with half of his companions, prayed the fear prayer. Zuhayr and Said b. Abdullah al-Hanefi passed in front of him and became a barrier. Said met his imam's arrows with his own body and did not move until the prayer was over. When the prayer was finished, Said fell to the ground, thirteen arrows piercing his body.

scenes.18.text: In the afternoon, Ali Akbar asked his father for permission to appear. He was the youngest son of Husayn and he was eighteen years old. He was the one who most resembled the Prophet in his face, voice and speech. Those who missed the Prophet looked to Ali Akbar to see him and hear his voice. He looked at his son for a long time, his eyes filled and he raised his hands to heaven and said, "O Allah, I complain to You about these. They're killing the boy who most resembles your Prophet". Ali Akbar rode his horse. When they saw a young man who looked so much like the Prophet in front of them, they were surprised. His sword shone in the sun and he struck many times. Finally, arrows and spears surrounded him. Wounded, he returned to his father's arms and was martyred. He slowly dropped his son on the ground. When the women in the tent saw her in this condition, they cried out with a heartbreaking scream.

scenes.19.text: Then **Hasan**'s son came to his uncle. He was young, just a kid. He asked his uncle for permission to fight. His Holiness did not agree at first, but His Holiness Kasem insisted. Then Husayn asked him, "My son, how do you see death?" "Death in the cause of Allah is sweeter to me than honey", said the Prophet. He gave permission for his nephew to fight. When the little boy appeared, the sword he was holding was large for his height. The army he faced didn't spare a child. Mubarak was struck by Ibn Fudayl al-Eddi and fell from his horse. It's said he called out to his uncle when he fell. Husayn grew up quickly and put his nephew on his lap. He carried the body himself and laid it with the martyrs of the Hashemites.

scenes.20.text: In the tents, the girls were crying out of thirst. "Water, uncle, water!" they called out to **Abbas**. The flag of the army was in the hands of Abbas. He was one of the strongest warriors of the Hashemites. His father bore the courage and sword strength of Ali. He couldn't stand the screams of the children any longer. He took an empty whip on his shoulder and rode his horse to the Euphrates. Hundreds of horsemen were guarding the riverbank. Abbas jumped in between them. He was swinging his sword on one side and his horse on the other. The ranks in front of him were scattered before him. Every step he took was a struggle, wounds on his body, but he didn't stop. Finally, he led the enemy into battle and reached the banks of the Euphrates. He got off his horse and dipped his hand in the cool water. He's been thirsty for days. He took water in his hand and brought it close to his lips. At that moment, he remembered that his brother Husayn and the children in the tent were thirsty. He spilled the water back into the river without drinking it. He filled it to the brim, hit it on the shoulder, and headed for the tent. This time, the enemy cut the way back. One of the ambushers behind the palm trees cut off his right arm with a sudden blow. Abbas stumbled, but he didn't let go of the whip. He took the whip in his left hand to his mouth and gripped it tightly with his teeth. Then he grabbed the sword in his left hand from his right hand, which had fallen to the ground. He kept driving his horse towards the tents with the sword in his left hand between his fangs. He was one-handed against those who went before him, his eyes were on the tents. A short time later, another blow cut off his left arm. He no longer had a hand to hold a sword or an arm to grasp a whip. Still, he kept the whip in his mouth and pushed forward. This time, they shot at him. One of the arrows pierced the whip, and all the water it carried for the children spilled out. Abbas's last hope went down with that water. Then an arrow went through his eye. He fell off his horse with a blow. He ran to his brother's head. And when he saw it, he said, "Now my back is broken". Because Abbas was the standard-bearer of his army and the most trusted man of Husayn. His love for her was much deeper, much more loving than that of a brother.

scenes.21.text: After Abbas, a subtle crying sound came from the tent. Zaynab brought the baby, who hadn't seen the water for three days, to Husayn. This was a six-month-old baby, **Ali Asgar**. Her lips were dry, she didn't even have the strength to cry. He took the baby in his arms, went out in front of the army and held it up for all to see, saying, "What did this child do to you? Give her a sip of water". Some of the soldiers turned their heads. At that time Harmala b. al-Kahil drew his bow and the arrow he fired pierced the baby's throat. His Highness Ali Asgar fell into his father's arms and soon became motionless. Husayn's hands were filled with his baby's blood. He sprinkled the blood toward the sky, and not a drop of it fell to the ground. The angels were not pleased that the innocent infant's blood should be shed on the ground, and they lifted him up from the air to heaven. And he lifted up his eyes to heaven and said, "O Allah, accept this offering from us. It is the fact that he is in your presence that has eased my affliction". Then she pressed the baby to her chest and quietly led him back to the tent. The women in the tent began to cry.

scenes.22.text: In the afternoon, only Husayn was left in the square. His friends, his brothers, his sons and nephews were lying around the desert. Then he looked to his right and to his left, then he called out, "Is there no one to help us?" The sound reached the tents. The sick son wanted to get out of bed, but the women held him back. He drew Husayn's sword and fought an army alone. Finally, his body filled with sores and he fell from his horse. And when he fell down prostrate, he submitted. **Sinân** thrust his spear into him. The towel came close to cut off his head, but his hands trembled and he pulled back. Then Shimr got off his horse and killed the imam who was prostrating. The blessed one cut off his head from behind, from his thigh, separating him from his body. The blessed head of Husayn was attached to the spearhead along with the heads of the other martyrs. These heads are being prepared to be sent to Damascus to be taken to Yazid.

scenes.23.text: For a while, the desert was silent. The sound of the sword ceased, the screams ceased. As the dust slowly descended to the ground, the battlefield was exposed in its entirety. The blessed body of Husayn was on the ground. **Abbas** lay on the banks of the Euphrates with his arms cut off. Ali Akbar, **Kasim** and the other sons of Hashim stood side by side where Husayn was carrying them with his own hands. The women and children in the tents looked out from the curtain. Zaynab stood up and took the children in her arms. The patient was lying in the bed of His Holiness Zayn al-Abidin. This silence was not a triumphant silence. Even the soldiers of the opposing army couldn't look each other in the face for a while.
scenes.23.art.actors.0.label: 1sxy6lc

scenes.24.text: The silence was broken by Umar b. Sa'd's voice. He turned to his soldiers and said, "Who will step on Husayn's chest and his back with his horses?" Ten horsemen have volunteered. They rode their horses over the Prophet's kissed chest and his grandson's back. The blessed body was crushed under the buttocks of the horses. The dust rose, and the blood mingled with the soil. The women in the tents wept at the sight. This atrocity against a man who lost his life showed how humiliated Yazidi's army was. The body that had just bowed was now the scene of an army's outrage.
scenes.24.art.actors.1.label: 17b9rtg

scenes.25.text: Then the soldiers attacked the tents. They ransacked, set fire to the tents. They forced the earrings off the little girls' ears. As the children fled from the flames, Zaynab gathered them one by one. In one of the tents, Zaynab was still lying in the flames. One of the soldiers asked, "Should we kill this patient too?" **Humeyd b. Muslim** intervened and tried to dissuade them. At that time, Zaynab came to his nephew and confronted the soldiers. He wouldn't let them kill him. When the soldiers heard this, they withdrew, saying, "He is not worthy to be killed". Finally , Umar b. Sa'd has ordered that the sick young man not be touched. Thus, the descendants of Husayn survived thanks to the courage of his aunt Zaynab. The slavery started in those burned tents.

scenes.26.text: Before the day of Ashura ends, Umar b. Sa'd sent the blessed head of Husayn to Haveli and **Humeyd** and Kufa, to **Ibn Ziyad**. The heads of the other martyrs were also collected. And they set forward, and with them went Shimri, and Kayish, and **Amr**, seventy-two. According to Ahl-i Beyt's legend, the head was attached to the tip of the spear. The faces of those who prayed at the Prophet's grandson's side the day before were now being carried away like the spoils of an army. As the horsemen advanced toward Kufa, spearheads appeared in a row on the desert horizon. In the desert of Karbala, the bodies of the martyrs were left in the sun.

scenes.27.text: The next day, the prisoners were released. Husayn's daughters, sisters, wives, children and sick Husayn were put on camels. When the caravan left Karbala, it passed by the place where the martyrs lay. And all the women wept as they looked upon the bodies of their brethren, and of their sons, and of their husbands, upon the camels. Zaynab didn't leave his nephew for a moment. He grabbed the young imam's head, his fever was still high, and tried to protect him from the bumps in the road. The spearheads were going in front of the convoy. The children would occasionally raise their heads and look at those spears, then bury their faces in their aunts' skirts. Days later, the walls of the Dome appeared on the horizon.
scenes.27.art.actors.0.label: 1sxy6lc
Lady Zaynab
scenes.28.text: The streets in Kufa were crowded. From the windows and rooftops, curious faces stared at the prison convoy. The people of this city, who just a few months ago wrote a letter to Husayn saying "Come", now saw his family as captives. According to Ahl-i Beyt's stories, the heads of the martyrs were carried in the streets with spear points. Some squinted, some cried secretly, some watched as if nothing had happened. Zaynab stood upright on the camels. He was with his sick nephew. Most of the letter writers were content to look out their windows that day. Not a hand was extended to the Prophet's family in this city.
scenes.28.art.actors.1.label: 1sxy6lc
Lady Zaynab
scenes.29.text: After the Kufa, the road turned to Damascus. Zaynab, the sick Zaynab, the women and children were put on camels. To ride for days on a camel without you was a pain in the bones. They did this to humiliate the Prophet's family and to torment them. The desert sun burned during the day, and the cold worked on the joints at night. Little children were trying not to fall, clinging to the camels' hairy backs. Zaynab watched over his children and nephew at night. He gave his little portion of food to the little ones. As the convoy passed through the towns, people lined the roadside to watch the prisoners. At the end of the long journey, the gates of Damascus were visible.
scenes.29.art.actors.0.label: 1sxy6lc
Lady Zaynab
scenes.29.art.actors.1.label: ms2fd7
Imam Zayn al-Abidin
scenes.30.text: While the prisoners were being taken to Damascus, two young boys were left in Kufa prison. These were Muhammad and Abraham, the sons of Muslim b. Aqil. People remember them as Tiflan-i-Muslim, the children of the Muslim. For a year, they were kept in a dark cell. Finally, during the night, a jailer opened the doors and let them out. Two brothers knocked on the door of a house in the dark. The woman who answered the door gave them food and a place to sleep. But when the woman's husband, Harris, came home, he recognized the children. He knew Ibn Ziyad had a reward for them. At night, he led them to the banks of the Euphrates. The children asked permission to pray before they died. And they abstained, and they prayed, and they embraced. Harris killed them both. When the news reached Ibn Ziyad, he punished the reward-seeking **Haris**.
scenes.30.art.actors.0.label: 1en5zur
Muhammad
scenes.30.art.actors.1.label: 114ijvk
Ibrahim
scenes.30.art.actors.2.label: 1ngjwez
al-Harith
scenes.31.text: At the end of the days' journey, the convoy reached Damascus. Without you, the prisoners on camels were brought to Yazid's lighted palace. The council was packed. The blessed head of Husayn was placed before Yazid. Yazid started hitting her lips with his stick. Abu Berze, one of the companions in the council, could not bear it and objected: "I have seen the Messenger of Allah kiss this face many times before". That's when Zaynab stood up. He was in chains, but the voice reached all corners of the council, "This head in your hand is the head of the Prophet's grandson". The palace was silent for a moment. Yazid thought he was celebrating the victory, but what everyone remembered from that meeting were the words of Zaynab.
scenes.31.art.actors.0.label: y5wmss
Zaynab
scenes.31.art.actors.1.label: 1f4krkm
Yazid
scenes.32.text: Yazid wanted to show everyone in the parliament his victory. But when Zaynab stood up, the council went elsewhere. Ibn Ziyad asked him mockingly, "What did you see Allah do to your brother and your family?" And Zaynab said to him, "I saw nothing but beauty". Now he was standing in front of Yazid with the same glory. And he praised Allah and saluted the Prophet and his household. Then he turned straight to Yazid and said, "O Yazid! Thou hast shut the doors of heaven and earth against us, and hast dragged us captive from city to city. Do you think that by this we are worthless and you are valuable to God? You think you've won, but you're the loser". Then he mentioned to him his offspring, saying, "O son of the one who was liberated in the conquest of Makkah! You kept your wives and your concubines behind a curtain, and you took captive the daughters of the Messenger of Allah, and you made them wander from city to city in public. Is this your justice?" He did not forget the stick he struck on the head of Husayn: "You strike the lips of the master of the youth of Paradise and in doing so you call their ancestors. You will go to them and say, "Would that my hand were dry and my tongue dumb". He said, "O my people, if you were to listen to me, you would not be able to destroy us, and you would not be able to destroy what we have revealed to you". You tried to extinguish the light of the Ahl al-Bayt, but you failed". And he said, "All praise is due to Allah, Who has set a seal on us with goodness, and a seal on us with goodness". Yazid didn't know what to say. He was silent in front of a female prisoner in the assembly, who he thought he had won. The Prophet's granddaughter, the daughter of Ali, spoke with her father's voice that day. This sermon went beyond the palace walls. For days, the palace residents talked among themselves about these things, and then the whole city of Damascus started talking about it. People heard from Zaynab that what was celebrated as victory was actually a disgrace.
scenes.32.art.actors.0.label: 1sxy6lc
I 'm sorry about that .
scenes.32.art.actors.1.label: 1f4krkm
Yazid
scenes.33.text: After the assembly, the Yazidi imprisoned the prisoners in a ruined building in Damascus. The walls were damp and it was freezing in the night. Among the captives was Hasan Husayn's four-year-old daughter, Hasan **Rukayye**. Every night, he cried, "Where's my dad?" Zaynab was holding her and comforting her. One night, Hazrat Rukayye saw his father in a dream, and as soon as he woke up, he started to cry. His voice was heard as far as the palace. Yazid said, "What's going on, what's all this crying about?" I said to him, Husayn's little daughter wants her father, she's crying for him". And Yazid commanded, and said, Carry his father's head to him, that he may see his father. The blessed head of Husayn was sent to Husayn Rukayye in a basket covered with a cloth. He lifted the veil and saw his father's face. He pressed his head to his chest and said, "Daddy, who painted you with blood?" And he laid his lips upon his father's face, and he gave up his spirit.
scenes.33.art.actors.1.label: y5wmss
Zaynab
scenes.34.text: To cover up Karbala, the Amish tried to make Ashura a day of celebration and fertility. Ashure dessert was popularized for this purpose. Today, unfortunately, this has been very successful: when people think of Ashura, they don't think of Karbala, they think of sweetness. The Assyrian belief that the food left over from Noah's Ark and cooked to commemorate his salvation would bring blessings to the house on that day, the reward of taking a bath on that day, and the eye will not ache for the rest of the year is not a solid one. They're all unfounded superstitions. Ibn Taymiyyah says that the gosul and driving tales were invented by the Nasibs who were fighting the Ahl-i Beyt.
scenes.34.art.actors.1.label: 1f4krkm
Yazid
scenes.35.text: Centuries have passed over Karbala, but the names of the martyrs have not been forgotten. The fortieth day of the martyrdom of Husayn is called Erbain and every year on this day millions of people march to Karbala. Food and water are offered to hikers in tents along the way. According to the official announcement of the tomb of Abbas in Karbala, 21,480,525 visitors visited Karbala during Erbain's visit in 2024. According to official Saudi data, the number of pilgrims that year was 1,833,164. That's ten times the number of people who flock to Karbala in Erbain.
scenes.36.text: Yazid conquered the Karbala desert that day, but he couldn't conquer the Prophet's religion. The non-beatification of Husayn showed everyone that Islam is not a toy of a ruling family. The waters of the Euphrates are dried up, the tents are burned, the blessed capital is moved from city to city. But while Yazid's name was remembered with a curse, Husayn's name continued to be remembered with tears on every Muharram. **Abbas** was the name of loyalty, youth resembling the Prophet Ali Akbar, **Kasim** loyalty, **Ali Asgar** innocence. Zaynab's words in the Damascus palace are still remembered. Shiites commemorate Karbala every year in mourning processions, mourning and visitations. Visitors who come to the tomb bow their heads and greet him: "Assalamu alaikum o Eba Abdillahi-l-Husayn".
scenes.36.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
sunni.0.says: Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn are the masters of the youth of Paradise.
sunni.1.says: At Umar b. Sa'd's call, ten men trample Imam Husayn with horses, and his chest and back are crushed. The girls, the sisters and the sick Imam Zayn al-Abidin are taken to Kufa.
sunni.2.says: Yazid has a stick in his hand and strikes Imam Husayn's teeth. Abu Barza objects. The page varies by edition.
sunni.2.grade: The sentence is quoted in the history books.
sunni.3.says: The cutting off of the water, the killing and the caravan of captives are also told in these histories.
sunni.4.says: On the evening of Thursday the 9th of Muharram, Shimr calls Abbas, Ja'far and Uthman "the sons of my sister" and gives them safe-conduct. The young men say, "May God curse you and your safe-conduct." There is no safe-conduct for the son of the Messenger of God.
sunni.5.says: They pray the noon prayer. Imam Husayn leads the fear prayer. In the afternoon the fighting intensifies and the army reaches him. Al-Hanafi steps forward, arrows rain to the right and left, and he stands until he falls. Zuhayr also fights beside him.
sunni.5.grade: On this page there is no order "shoot them with arrows, let him not pray," nor shield, shoulder or leg.
shia.0.says: Al-Hurr stops the caravan with a thousand horsemen. Imam Husayn gives water to them and their horses.
shia.1.says: On the morning of Ashura al-Hurr chooses Paradise, comes to Imam Husayn and apologizes for having held him on the road.
shia.2.says: Abbas sends forward his brothers of the same mother. They are martyred. Imam Husayn heads for the Euphrates, with Abbas in front of him. The army cuts Abbas off. He fights alone and is killed.
shia.2.grade: The cutting off of the arms, the water-skin and the eye are not on this page. They belong to the maqtal narrative.
shia.3.says: An arrow of Harmala b. al-Kahil lodges in the baby's throat. Zaynab asks for water. In another version the baby has been thirsty for three days and Imam Husayn calls out to the army for a sip of water.
shia.4.says: In the assembly in Damascus Yazid strikes Imam Husayn's teeth with a stick. Zaynab stands up, and her voice resounds through the assembly. The head is before Yazid.
shia.5.says: Abbas's tearing up and throwing away the safe-conduct paper, the heads being put on spears and paraded, and Zaynab's throwing herself over the sick Imam Zayn al-Abidin are told in these maqtals. Lady Zaynab was not ill. Abbas's not drinking the water, the cutting off of his arms, the arrow to the water-skin and the eye; the martyrdom of the young men; and the tearing off of the girls' earrings are also here. The portrait of the standard-bearer and the strongest arm is the maqtal's naming.
shia.5.grade: Ahl-i Bayt is a mektel narrative. There is no closure on Zaynab in al-Irshad 2/113. There Humeyd will repel the troops.
shia.6.says: On the evening of Thursday the 9th of Muharram Shimr says to Abbas, Ja'far and Uthman, "You are under safe-conduct." The young men curse the safe-conduct. There is no safe-conduct for the son of the Messenger of God.
shia.6.grade: On this page there is no tearing of the paper. The tearing is a maqtal narrative.
shia.7.says: Shimr calls the sons of Umm al-Banin and tells them of obedience to Yazid b. Mu'awiya. Abbas refuses to abandon Imam Husayn, the son of Fatima, and curses the safe-conduct that was brought. The editor's note refers to Abbas as Qamar Bani Hashim and writes that the banner was with him.
shia.7.grade: Qamar Bani Hashim, the banner and the name Umm al-Banin are in the editor's note on p. 148. The note refers to Maqatil al-Talibiyyin. It is not Ibn Tawus's own sentence.
shia.8.says: Imam Zayn al-Abidin says that on the evening of the morning his father would be killed he sat ill and his aunt Zaynab looked after him.
shia.9.says: Sinan thrusts the spear. Khawli trembles. Shimr slaughters Imam Husayn and gives the head to Khawli. The women's veils are pulled off their backs. The page cuts off at Imam Zayn al-Abidin on his bed.
shia.10.says: Imam Zayn al-Abidin is gravely ill. "Shall we kill this sick man?" is said. Humayd turns them back. Umar b. Sa'd says the sick child is not to be touched. Then ten men trample the body with a horse. The same day the head is sent with Khawli and Humayd to Ibn Ziyad. The other seventy-two heads are sent with Shimr, Qays and Amr.
shia.10.grade: Putting on a spear and parading is not on this page. That is the maqtal narrative.
shia.11.says: Imam Husayn's four-year-old daughter sees her father in a dream and weeps. Yazid sends the head to her. In the short narrative the girl falls ill and dies in Damascus within a few days. In the extended narrative on the same page, the head is covered with a handkerchief and placed in a basin. The cover is lifted. The girl takes the head to her chest, pours out her sorrow with "Father, who stained you with blood," presses her lip to her father's lip, and gives up her soul there.
shia.11.grade: It is an Ahl al-Bayt maqtal narrative. On this page the girl's name and the ruin of Damascus do not appear. The maqtal calls her Ruqayya and the place a ruin. The note ties the narrative to Kamil-i Baha'i, vol. 2, pp. 178-179.
shia.12.says: Relays from Kamil-i Baha'i. The children are told their father is on a journey. Yazid takes them into his house. The four-year-old girl sees her father in a dream. Yazid sends the head into her lap. The girl falls ill and dies in Damascus within a few days.
shia.12.grade: It is an Ahl al-Bayt maqtal narrative. On this page the name is not Ruqayya. The ruin, the tray and the dying there while pouring out her sorrow are not here. They are in the extended narrative in Nafas al-Mahmum.
shia.13.says: Nafas al-Mahmum and Muntaha al-Amal tie the narrative of this little girl to Kamil-i Baha'i. Nafas's note shows vol. 2, pp. 178-179.
shia.13.grade: Ahl al-Bayt is a legend. The number shown on the note was not given as the page of the Perfect.
shia.14.says: At noon Imam Husayn places Zuhayr and Sa'id in front of him with half of the remaining companions and prays the fear prayer. An arrow hits Imam Husayn. Sa'id covers him with his body and falls without moving. On his body are thirteen arrows, as well as sword and spear wounds.
shia.14.grade: Shoulder, leg and shield are not on this page. The "shoot them" order is not either.
shia.15.says: Abu Thumama reminds him of the prayer. Imam Husayn says the first time, and asks the enemy to stop for the prayer. Husayn b. Numayr says "it will not be accepted." Habib answers. Zuhayr and Sa'id step forward. Sa'id becomes a target of arrows and falls martyred with thirteen arrows.
shia.15.grade: The words "he has left the religion" and the order "shoot them, let him not pray" are not on this page. The sentence on the page is that the prayer will not be accepted.
shia.16.says: The commanders call out to the soldiers to shoot them with arrows and not let them pray. The companions shield with shields and their bodies. They take arrows in the shoulder and leg and do not move so that the prayer will not be broken. Imam Husayn is portrayed as having left the religion.
shia.16.grade: Ahl al-Bayt is a legend. It is the same with the Qur'an. 165 and Bihar 45/21 don't list those three details.
shia.17.says: It is narrated that Husayn said to Walid: "Yazid is a pervert, a drunkard, a murderer of innocent souls whom Allah has made untouchable.
shia.18.says: Yazid's drinking and monkey fun is commemorated on this date.
shia.19.says: The exodus from Medina, the letters to the Kufa, the abandonment of the Muslim, the Ashura speech and the exodus of the companions one by one are narrated in this text.
shia.20.says: When Husayn lifted his oath on the 9th night of Muharram and told them to use the night like a camel, some of them left in the dark, the Bedouins who came in the hope of spoil were scattered by the fall of Kufa and the martyrdom of Muslim. In these books, Avsece and Zuhayr say that they will not separate even if they are resurrected a thousand times, the appearance of Hz. November and the mention of the name of Karbala as kerb and bela.
shia.21.says: The reward of visiting the land of Karbala and remembering Husayn is summarized in this work.
shia.22.says: It is reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) had announced that the place where Husayn would be martyred would be called Karbala, and that he entrusted the land that Gabriel had brought to Ummu Seleme and said that when this land became blood, Husayn would be martyred.
shia.23.says: It is mentioned in the Bihari'l-Enwar that Husayn bought the land of Karbala from the people of Nineveh and Gadiriyah for 60,000 dirhams, and then gave the land as a charity to those who visited his tomb, on the condition that they guide them and host them for three days.
shia.24.says: After Karbala, Muslim b. It is narrated that Aqil's two sons Muhammad and Ibrahim were held in the Kufa prison, a prisoner released them, they took refuge at night in the house of a woman, her husband Haris took them to the Euphrates bank for the reward of Ibn Ziyad, the brothers were martyred after praying and hugging each other, and Ibn Ziyad punished Haris.
shia.25.says: When he was caught, he asked for cold water at the palace door. That Amr didn't give a drop, then Amr b. It says on this page that Hureys had water brought and that he couldn't drink it because of the wound in his mouth. It's not on this page that he called the ring water during the war.
shia.26.says: It is said that he did not participate in the war because of his illness, that those who wanted to kill him were told that the disease would be enough for him, and that he was taken captive to Kufa and Damascus. There's nothing on this page about Zaynab being sick.
shia.27.says: It is said that Ibn Fudayl struck al-Ezdi in the head, split his head, called out to his uncle and that Husayn put him on his chest and placed him with the martyrs of the Hashemites. It doesn't say the severed head was moved at that time.
shia.28.says: According to the official announcement of the Turbe, 21,480,525 visitors came to Karbala during the 2024 Erbain visit.
shia.29.says: The 2024 Hajj count is 1,833,164 people. This is the Hajj only. It is not visits to the Kaaba throughout the year, nor umra.
disputes.0.title: 1wqh2gq
Why was the pledge of allegiance refused?
disputes.0.sunni: That Imam Husayn did not pledge allegiance to Yazid is written in the histories. Some regard his rising as an ijtihad. His martyrdom is not denied.
disputes.0.shia: The refusal is due to Yazid's incompetence. He ruled the Mu'awiya Caliphate, forcibly placed his son, who was remembered for drinking, in charge. His Holiness did not bow to this order. Abbas refused the trust, considering it obedience to Yazid.
disputes.1.title: hinl8d
The stick, the horses and the heads
disputes.1.sunni: The horses' trampling of the body is in al-Tabari, vol. 5, p. 455. The sending of the head to Kufa is in al-Irshad, vol. 2, p. 113. The stick scene is also mentioned in al-Tabari; some scholars regard the head's going to Damascus as weak.
disputes.1.shia: The horses, the heads on spears and the stick are read as the shame of Yazid's assembly. Zaynab's sermon is delivered in this assembly (Bihar, vol. 45, p. 134). The maqtal ties the same tyranny to Ruqayya's martyrdom in the ruin as well (Nafas al-Mahmum, vol. 1, p. 416).
questions.0: Husayn looked at the governor of Medina and said, "No one like me would betray someone like him". Why do you think Husayn refused to pledge allegiance to Yazid's rule?
questions.1: And Zimri gave the deed of surety to Abbas and to his brethren; and Abbas rent the deed, and cast it away. Why do you think Abbas didn't let Husayn go when he was offered life?
questions.2: The Hürr did not draw his sword in the first encounter, but he did not back down from his orders. Why do you think the Hürr changed ranks when the war was about to begin?
questions.3: When Husayn asked for a break for the noon prayer, the commanders of the opposing side said, "Raise the arrows and let them not pray". Why do you think the commanders were afraid of Husayn praying?
questions.4: Abbas took the water of the Euphrates in his hand, but without drinking it, he poured it into the river. Why do you think Abbas hasn't drunk water in days when he's been thirsty?
questions.5: Husayn picked up Ali Asgar, six months old, and asked, "What did this child do to you? Give her a sip of water". Why do you think Husayn put the baby in front of the army where everyone could see it?
questions.6: Zaynab stood up in the council of Yazid with her chains in hand and called out to him, "O son of those freed in the conquest of Mecca!" Why do you think Zaynab reminded Yazid of her ancestry?
questions.7: When Rukayye cried out, "Where is my father?" Yazid ordered that Husayn's head be brought to him. Why do you think Yazid made a four-year-old do that?
summary: Husayn did not pledge allegiance to Yazid. 9 On the evening of Muharram, Shimr, Abbas and his brothers offered him a pledge, but they refused. The water's out. The midday prayer of terror was offered, and Said was mortally wounded by thirteen arrows. Alamdar Abbas, Hz Ali Akber, Hz Kasım and Hz Ali Asgar were martyred. The patient stayed in the tent. The blessed head of Hasan Kasim was split open; Husayn laid his body beside the sons of Hashim. Muslim motherfucker . Aqil's orphans were martyred on the banks of the Euphrates after being released from Kufa prison. Shimr struck the final blow, and the horses trampled on the corpse. The heads went to Ibn Ziyad in Kufa, and from there to Yazid in Damascus. In the letter, Hz. Rukayye grabs his father's head in the ruins and is martyred there. The common sentences are in Tabari 5/416, Tabari 5/441, Tabari 5/455 and Tirmizi 3768. The details are in the Book of the People of the House.
key: No pledge to Yazid: the safe-conduct refused, the ten days of Karbala
notes.0: Mu'awiya left the caliphate to his son Yazid. Imam Husayn refused this pledge.
notes.1: 9 On the evening of Muharram, Shimr, Abbas and his brothers extended their hands. They rejected the trust and cursed it. 150).
notes.2: Al-Hurr stopped the caravan; on the morning of Ashura he repented and went over to Imam Husayn's ranks (al-Irshad, vol. 2, pp. 78 and 99).
notes.3: The prayer of fear was said in the afternoon of Ashura. Sa'id became a bulwark to Husayn with his body (Tabari 5/441, al-Luhruf p. 165, Bihar 45/21).
notes.4: The water was cut off. The standard-bearer Abbas reached the river. Ali al-Asghar was struck by Harmala's arrow (al-Luhuf, p. 169).
notes.5: His Highness was ill. Zaynab was waiting at the top. They wanted to kill him in the tent.
notes.6: The heads were sent to Ibn Ziyad in Kufa on the same day (al-Irshad 2/113). From there it was transported to Yazid in Damascus (Bihar, vol. 45, p. 134).
notes.7: Zaynab, the sick Zayn al-Abidin, the women and children were taken from Kufa to Damascus on unmounted camels.
notes.8: In the maqtal, Ruqayya clings to her father's head in the ruin of Damascus and is martyred there (Nafas al-Mahmum, vol. 1, p. 416).
notes.9: On the night of 9 Muharram, Husayn lifted his beatification. There were those who walked in the dark. The rest of us said we wouldn't split even if we were resurrected a thousand times.
notes.10: Muslim motherfucker . Aqil's orphans Muhammad and Ibrahim were martyred on the banks of the Euphrates after being imprisoned in Kufa.
notes.11: In 63 AH Medina was plundered for three days at al-Harra. In 64 AH the Kaaba was pelted with stones from catapults and its covering burned. Yazid died at this time.

sunni.6.says: Walid's request for a bead and Husayn's night departure from Medina; Muslim b. Aqil's being alone, asking for water and being killed; the lifting of the beath on the night of Ashura and the answers of the companions; the story of the sickness of Zayn al-Abidin that night and the fact that his aunt Zaynab looked after him; the Ashura sermon; the testimony of Habib, Zuhayr, Ali Akber, Kasim and Abbas; Sinân and Havliy; the looting of tents and the sick Ali b. Not touching Husayn, passing the prisoners by the martyrs, and the heads going around the Kufa.
sunni.6.grade: The narratives of Abu Mihnef come through Tabari. Sunni hadith scholars consider Abu Mihnef weak, but Sunni historians transmit these narratives.
sunni.7.says: It is narrated that Jibril brought to the Prophet the land where Husayn would be killed and that this land was entrusted to Umm Salamah; it is narrated that Ali wept while passing through Karbala on the way to Siffin.
sunni.8.says: According to Ibn Taymiyyah, there is no authentic tradition for washing, dressing, decorating, burning linen, celebrating and cooking Ashura; the tradition of "he who draws the linen will not perish" and "he who is not sick in the year of good" was invented by the Nassib who rebelled against the Ahl-i Beyt; that the Umayyads accepted that day as a holiday to make them forget Karbala.
sunni.8.grade: I 'm going to have to go back to school .
shia.30.says: In the assembly of Yazid, Zaynab begins to praise Allah, reproaches Yazid as the son of those who were freed, asks for the captivity of the daughters of the Prophet and says, "Do whatever you will, Allah cannot erase our name, you cannot kill our revelation". In the Qur'an, Ibn Ziyad is quoted as saying, "I saw nothing but beauty".
